svg.title: Uniform physical transfer through resistor faces
svg.desc: Resistor-only elimination retains at most ten vertices and forty-five resistor slots. A maximum-conductance spanning forest has at most nine edges. An empty scale band permits small total-budget opening and contraction while leaving a bounded resistor backbone. A tiny natural driven denominator yields a nearby physical internal mode; a regular denominator yields a repaired zero-loss driven state and a global near-target core chart. The written bound is error greater than ten to the negative power ten to the forty-fifth. It is an extremely small structural bound; a practical global margin, independent review and full formal verification remain open.
svg.text: A physical transfer argument through every resistor face
1. Retain both terminals and every reactive endpoint
Resistor-only elimination gives at most 10 vertices, 45 R slots and the same LC branches.
A maximum-conductance R spanning forest has at most 9 edges.
2. Use an empty backbone scale band
Short strong tree edges; open weak cuts; retain small redundant R edges inside components.
The surviving backbone controls natural coefficient floors and voltage-level clustering.
Small source denominator
Repair an approximate internal mode.
Change only positive LC values.
KCL holds at every original node.
Exact-mode sample error > 10⁻¹³.
Regular source denominator
Repair a zero-loss unit-current state.
Recover the two core response charts.
No supplied component box is assumed.
Near-target chart error > 1/300.
Uniform structural conclusion for at most four reactives
Arbitrary finite resistor count and values.
The bound is extremely small. A practical-sized global margin remains open.
Written project self-review; independent and full formal assurance remain separate. Selected Lean count: 41.
